name: Yellohu for WooCommerce
author: Yellohu

sections.description:
Yellohu for WooCommerce connects your store to Yellohu, the Italian platform to compare and buy shipments with the main couriers (BRT, Poste Italiane, UPS, FedEx, DHL Freight, InPost, PalletWays and more).

Your WooCommerce orders arrive in your Yellohu account by themselves. There you pick the courier, pay and print the label, and the tracking number goes back to the order in your store.

The plugin is optional: Yellohu also works with WooCommerce through the standard REST API alone. The plugin adds the tools you see inside WordPress:

  • One-click connection: connect the store from WooCommerce > Yellohu, no keys to copy.
  • Yellohu column in the orders list, with the Yellohu status (“Ready”, “To complete”, “Shipped”, “Shipped outside Yellohu”, “Cancelled”) and the tracking number, plus a filter by Yellohu status.
  • “Send to Yellohu” bulk action and a “Ship with Yellohu” button on the order screen. Orders that cannot be shipped (already completed, cancelled, without an address, with virtual products only) are skipped and the reason is shown.
  • Product fields for shipping: HS code, country of origin and shipment type (parcel, pallet, documents) on every product and variation, used for customs on non-EU shipments.
  • No duplicate emails: when Yellohu sends the tracking, the “order completed” email can be left to Yellohu.

The plugin is thin: it stores no customer data of its own and the shipping logic runs on Yellohu. It supports HPOS (custom order tables) and the checkout blocks.

The plugin interface is in Italian, the language of the Yellohu service.

A Yellohu account is required: you can create one for free at yellohu.com. You pay only for the shipments you buy.

External services

This plugin connects to the Yellohu service, operated by IntermediaBox S.r.l. (Italy), which is needed to import orders and create shipments. Nothing is sent until you connect the store.

  • Connection (app.yellohu.com): when you press “Connect to Yellohu”, your browser opens the Yellohu dashboard with your store address, so you can confirm the connection. WooCommerce then shows its standard screen to approve REST API access for Yellohu.
  • Sending orders (yellohu.com): when you use “Send to Yellohu” or “Ship with Yellohu”, the plugin sends the ids of the selected orders to Yellohu, signed with a secret shared at connection time. Yellohu then reads those orders from your store through the WooCommerce REST API you approved.
  • Disconnection (yellohu.com): when you deactivate or uninstall the plugin, it notifies Yellohu so that Yellohu stops writing to your store.

Yellohu also writes the Yellohu status, the tracking number and a link to the order in Yellohu as order meta, through the WooCommerce REST API.

  • Terms and conditions: https://yellohu.com/termini-e-condizioni
  • Privacy policy: https://yellohu.com/privacy-policy
sections.installation:
1. Install the plugin from Plugins > Add New, or upload the yellohu-for-woocommerce folder to /wp-content/plugins/.
  2. Activate it. WooCommerce must be active.
  3. Go to WooCommerce > Yellohu and press “Collega a Yellohu” (Connect to Yellohu), then approve the connection.
sections.faq:
Do I need a Yellohu account?

Yes. The plugin connects your store to your Yellohu account, where shipments are created and paid.

What data does the plugin send?

Only the ids of the orders you choose to send, plus a notice when the plugin is deactivated or uninstalled. Yellohu reads the order details from your store through the WooCommerce REST API you approved during the connection.

My store uses Cloudflare or a firewall.

Allow requests with the user agent Yellohu/1.0 or to paths starting with /wp-json/wc/, otherwise orders cannot be read. On Cloudflare also turn off Bot Fight Mode, which does not accept exceptions.

What happens if I deactivate the plugin?

Yellohu is notified and stops writing to your store. The HS code, origin and shipment type you saved on products stay in your store.
sections.changelog:
1.3.1

  • The settings page no longer loads fonts from Google: no request to third parties from the admin.

1.3.0

  • Renamed to Yellohu for WooCommerce (slug yellohu-for-woocommerce) for the WordPress.org plugin directory.
  • Readme in English with the external services section.

1.2.2

  • «Invia a Yellohu» dice quali ordini ha lasciato fuori e perché (già evasi, annullati, senza indirizzo, solo prodotti virtuali). Nella colonna Yellohu i nuovi stati «Spedito fuori da Yellohu» e «Annullato». / “Send to Yellohu” now reports skipped orders and why; new column states for orders shipped elsewhere and cancelled.

1.2.1

  • Sulla variante il tipo di spedizione vuoto si legge «Come il prodotto». / On variations an empty shipment type reads “Come il prodotto”.

1.2.0

  • Nuovo campo «Tipo di spedizione (Yellohu)» su prodotti e varianti: Pacco, Pallet o Documenti. Se lo lasci vuoto decide Yellohu. / New product and variation field: shipment type (parcel, pallet, documents).

1.1.3

  • Testi in italiano con le lettere accentate. / Italian copy with proper accents.

1.1.2

  • Pagina Yellohu ridisegnata a tutta larghezza, con stato del collegamento e fascia assistenza. / Redesigned full-width Yellohu page.

1.1.1

  • Data dell’ultimo ordine in formato breve, testo dei conteggi più chiaro, filtro dell’elenco ordini limitato agli ordini del negozio. / Short date format, clearer counter label, orders filter scoped to shop orders.

1.1.0

  • Nuova pagina Yellohu con lo stato del collegamento, l’account e gli ordini di oggi. Filtro Yellohu nell’elenco ordini e link all’etichetta quando c’è. / New Yellohu page, orders list filter and label link.

1.0.1

  • Dopo Scollega o Elimina da Yellohu il plugin non mostra più “Collegato”. Il pulsante Impostazioni apre la pagina WooCommerce. / Disconnecting from Yellohu now clears the link in the plugin.

1.0.0

  • Prima versione. / First release.
